reader.notes: Both REPLACE formats end in ExpectSeparatorPeriod, and every missing-period form probed at --std 85 is refused. When the period is missing and more text follows, the ellipsis in format 1 reads the next word as another operand, so the diagnostic is COBOL1641 'operand is not pseudo-text' rather than a missing period; --std 2023 gives the same. The refusal is right; only the wording could point to the period.

refuter.evidence: R1percomma-001 ('==W-B==.,' period not followed by a space) refused COBOL1641; R2cmtper-001 (the only period on a '*' comment line) refused; R5col73-001 (period only in column 73, the sequence area) refused; R7offsemi-001 ('REPLACE OFF.;') refused. Legal halves: R3eof-001 'REPLACE OFF.' as the last text with no line end compiled [BBB]; R4col72-001 period in column 72 with SEQ00001 in 73-80 compiled [BBB]; R6dbgper-001 the period on a debugging line without DEBUGGING MODE compiled [BBB], correct because §1985:VI.7.3 (cite.py OK) makes a debugging line a comment only 'After all COPY and REPLACE statements have been processed'. cite.py: OK §1985:XII.3.3 SR2.
